source: Climate Resilient Broadcasting Rice Growing Technique, ASPIRE/IFAD, MAFF, Feb 2018
text:
Once soil moisture is adequate, broadcast or transplanted rice seedlings emerge within 3-5 days. From there, raise the water level gradually as the crop ages: keep about 3-5cm depth when rice is 7-10 days old, then increase to about 20cm for short-duration varieties or 30cm for medium/heavy-duration varieties from tillering through to near maturity, draining the field before harvest.

If rainfall is insufficient or a dry spell hits, supplement with irrigation to keep the soil moist rather than letting the field dry out completely, since inconsistent water stresses the crop's growth. Where possible, build strong field bunds (ភ្លឺស្រែ) around each plot to hold water without over-flooding, and dig a small reservoir pond (roughly 20m x 10m) within the field to store a water reserve for short dry spells during the wet season. Small drainage channels along field edges help release excess water quickly if rainfall is unusually heavy, protecting the crop from both drought and waterlogging with the same set of structures.
